events.title: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New
events.what: The Lichtenstein retrospective brings together familiar Pop images and less-seen works, including recreations of four murals. An indoor art option that can pair with a walk through the Meatpacking District.
events.where: Whitney Museum · 99 Gansevoort Street
events.when: Oct 11, 2026–May 10, 2027 · closed Tuesdays; Fridays open until 10 p.m.
events.cost: Standard adult admission $30; ages 25 and under free. Check free-admission dates and reserve.
events.imageAlt: Roy Lichtenstein, Girl in Window, 1963; © Estate of Roy Lichtenstein, courtesy Whitney Museum

events.title: The Surrealist Book: Tomorrow Lives in Mirrors
events.what: Artists’ books, collage-filled sketchbooks and sculptural bindings show how Surrealists turned books into artworks. The exhibition includes work by Dalí, Cahun and Unica Zürn.
events.where: MoMA · Floor 3 · 11 West 53rd Street
events.when: Oct 4, 2026–Jan 23, 2027 · 10:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; Fridays until 8:30 p.m.
events.cost: Adult admission $30; special exhibitions included. NY State residents can reserve free Friday evening tickets.
events.imageAlt: Unica Zürn, Oracle and Spectacle, Book IV, 1960. MoMA; gift of Helen and Sam Zell. Photo: Ben Blackwell. © Verlag Brinkmann & Bose, Berlin.

events.title: Locating Girlhood at AFAM
events.where: American Folk Art Museum · 2 Lincoln Square
events.when: Oct 9–Feb 28 · Wed–Sun 11:30 a.m.–6 p.m.; closed Mon–Tue
events.cost: Free admission.
events.what: A new exhibition of roughly 100 works made by early American girls, including elaborate needlework, maps and painted objects. A compact, free art stop when you want something beyond shopping.
events.imageAlt: Needlework picture attributed to Faith Trumbull; Connecticut Museum / AFAM exhibition image

events.title: Outdoor skating at Rockefeller Center
events.when: Season open through March 27, 2027 · daily sessions; check the booking calendar
events.cost: Skating from $22; rental costs extra. Prices vary by session.
events.where: Midtown · Rockefeller Center
events.what: The outdoor rink is open for the season. Reserve a 60-minute session and check the arrival instructions on your ticket; session prices and availability vary.
events.imageAlt: The Rink at Rockefeller Center at night, organizer promotional photograph

events.title: Nuulee’s Mongolian cashmere pop-up
events.when: Oct 14–Dec 23; confirm daily shop hours
events.what: Browse Mongolian cashmere and winter knitwear at the temporary Nolita shop at 173 Elizabeth Street. Check the current shop hours before making a special trip.
events.where: 173 Elizabeth Street
events.cost: Items priced individually; admission charge not listed.
events.imageAlt: A model wears Nuulee’s pale-yellow cashmere and a blue patterned hat in the brand’s product photograph.

events.title: Jewel-toned paintings at 52 Walker
events.where: 52 Walker · 52 Walker Street
events.when: Nov 6–Dec 19 · opening reception Nov 6, 6–8 p.m.
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: Jem Perucchini’s Sospiro brings together luminous paintings and the first public presentation of his drawings. Renaissance imagery and African textiles inform the richly colored scenes; an intimate gallery stop rather than a museum-sized outing.
events.imageAlt: Jem Perucchini’s Sospiro, courtesy of the artist and Corvi-Mora, London

events.title: A tiny holiday chalet beside the rink
events.where: Rockefeller Center · enter from 49th Street
events.when: Nov 6–Jan 3 · reserved 50-minute visits; closed Dec 1–2.
events.cost: Reservations from $50, plus a $25 food-and-drink minimum per person; skating is separate.
events.what: Book a private rinkside chalet for up to six guests for 50 minutes. Two digital photographs are included; food and drinks come from 5 Acres. Enter from 49th Street and arrive 10 minutes early. Closed December 1–2 for tree-lighting preparations.
events.imageAlt: Decorated interior of a Rockefeller Center holiday chalet overlooking the rink; organizer photograph.

events.title: Grand Central’s indoor Holiday Fair
events.where: Vanderbilt Hall · 89 East 42nd Street
events.when: Nov 9–Dec 24 · November Mon–Sat 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; Sun 11 a.m.–6 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving.
events.cost: Free to browse; purchases optional.
events.what: Browse handmade jewelry, pottery, art and gifts beneath Vanderbilt Hall’s chandeliers. The indoor setting makes it a useful cold-weather market. Hours extend near Christmas; the organizer lists the later holiday schedule.
events.imageAlt: Grand Central’s main concourse with Holiday Fair banners in 2023; organizer photograph from an earlier season.

events.title: The Collective’s SoHo holiday market
events.where: 435 Broadway
events.when: Nov 1–Dec 31 · daily 11 a.m.–7 p.m.
events.cost: Free to browse; items individually priced.
events.what: An indoor holiday pop-up brings independent clothing, jewelry, candle and accessory brands together. Browse the stalls for smaller gifts, with no need to commit to a purchase or a fixed itinerary.
events.imageAlt: Shoppers browsing The Collective SoHo, photographed by the organizer

events.title: Grace Carney: To the Bone
events.where: P·P·O·W · 392 Broadway
events.when: Oct 30–Dec 19 · gallery Tue–Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m.
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: New paintings use layered marks and shifting forms to explore the body and its surroundings. A compact, free contemporary-art stop that can fit around a Tribeca walk; check holiday closures before visiting.
events.imageAlt: Grace Carney artwork photographed for P·P·O·W

events.title: Neue Galerie reopens with its masterworks
events.where: Neue Galerie · 1048 Fifth Avenue at 86th Street
events.when: Nov 12–Jan 11 · Wed–Mon 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; closed Tuesdays.
events.cost: $28 general admission; seniors $18; students and educators $15.
events.what: The museum’s 25th-anniversary display brings Austrian and German masterworks into its restored building, including Klimt’s Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I. The galleries have reopened; closed Tuesdays.
events.imageAlt: Gustav Klimt’s Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I, courtesy of Neue Galerie New York

events.title: The Holiday Train Show returns to NYBG
events.where: New York Botanical Garden · 2900 Southern Boulevard
events.when: Nov 14–Jan 10 · choose a timed admission.
events.cost: Paid All-Garden Pass; price varies by date and ticket type.
events.what: Miniature trains travel among nearly 200 New York landmarks made from botanical materials. Selected extended evenings begin November 27, with the displays lit after dark, live music and photo opportunities.
events.imageAlt: Miniature buildings and lush planting at NYBG’s Holiday Train Show

events.title: Union Square’s holiday market
events.where: Union Square Park
events.when: Nov 12–Dec 24 · Sun–Wed 11–8; Thu–Fri 11–9; Sat 10–9.
events.cost: Free to browse; food and shopping extra.
events.what: Nearly 200 vendors bring crafts, gifts and seasonal food to the park. Make it a browsing outing without a shopping commitment, or start a small holiday gift list.
events.imageAlt: A shopper browsing art prints at the Union Square Holiday Market

events.title: Ice-skating season at Wollman Rink
events.where: Wollman Rink · Central Park near East 59th Street
events.when: Season Oct 28–Mar 16 · Mon–Tue 10–2:30; Wed–Thu/Sun 10–9; Fri–Sat 10–10.
events.cost: Adult admission $16 off-peak, $28 peak or $40 prime; skate rental $12. Posted prices include tax.
events.what: A seasonal open-air skate beneath the skyline. Choose a less expensive session if your schedule allows, and check the booking calendar for weather changes and the date’s price category.
events.imageAlt: An aerial evening view of skaters at Wollman Rink

events.title: The Rockettes’ Christmas Spectacular
events.where: Radio City Music Hall · 1260 Sixth Avenue
events.when: Nov 4–Jan 4; select a performance time.
events.cost: Paid reserved seats; prices and fees vary by performance.
events.what: The Rockettes return to Radio City with precision dance, familiar holiday scenes and a new number with immersive effects. Compare seat prices and fees when choosing a performance.
events.imageAlt: The Rockettes pose together outdoors in sparkling silver costumes.

events.title: Gingerbread NYC: The Great Borough Bake-Off
events.where: Museum of the City of New York · 1220 Fifth Avenue
events.when: Nov 6–Jan 18 during museum hours; check holiday and private-event closures. Nov 18 closes at 2 p.m.
events.cost: Adult admission $23; NYC residents pay what they can with ID. Wednesday admission is free at the counter.
events.what: Explore edible interpretations of iconic New York buildings, made by bakers representing the five boroughs, and vote for a favorite. Holiday closures apply; free Wednesday admission is a specific offer, not the everyday price.
events.imageAlt: Visitors examine architectural gingerbread creations on long tables in the Museum of the City of New York.

events.title: Lightscape at Brooklyn Botanic Garden
events.where: Brooklyn Botanic Garden · 990 Washington Avenue
events.when: Selected evenings Nov 20–Jan 3; timed entry.
events.cost: Adults $29 value nights, $39 off-peak or $44 peak; fees included. Daytime garden admission does not include Lightscape.
events.what: Follow the outdoor illuminated trail through the garden. Book the date and entry window you want and dress for a long walk outside; daytime garden admission does not include this event.
events.imageAlt: Visitors walk beneath a tunnel of golden lights at Brooklyn Botanic Garden.

events.title: Bronx Zoo Holiday Lights
events.where: Bronx Zoo · 2300 Southern Boulevard
events.when: Public nights begin Nov 21; selected dates through Jan 3.
events.cost: Adult dated ticket $37.95; deal-day tickets from $29.95, any-night ticket $42.95. Optional train ride $4.
events.what: Animal lanterns and illuminated trails return with a new farmyard area. The organizer says a Holiday Lights ticket allows entry from 1 p.m., so check the selected date’s daytime and evening schedule before going.
events.imageAlt: An alpaca stands beneath colorful evening lights at the Bronx Zoo.

events.title: Shine Bright at Hudson Yards
events.where: The Shops & Restaurants at Hudson Yards
events.when: Nov 16–Jan 7; Shops hours generally Mon–Sat 10 a.m.–9 p.m., Sun 11 a.m.–7 p.m.
events.cost: Free to browse the lights; shopping, dining and Vessel admission are extra.
events.what: See the Great Room’s glowing hot-air-balloon centerpiece and the seasonal lighting across Hudson Yards. A good indoor option when the weather makes an outdoor lights walk less appealing.
events.imageAlt: The illuminated balloon installation and golden lights inside Hudson Yards.

events.title: Santa’s Winter Wonderland at Watermark
events.where: Watermark · Pier 15, 78 South Street
events.when: Nov 13–Dec 27; choose an available admission or dining slot.
events.cost: General admission starts at $18; heated-glasshouse dining has separate pricing.
events.what: The waterfront venue fills with Christmas trees and seasonal decorations. General admission is an outdoor visit with hot chocolate; a heated glasshouse meal is a separate reservation, so compare the two experiences before buying.
events.imageAlt: Santa poses amid Christmas decorations at Watermark on the waterfront.

events.title: Grand Central Thanksgiving Market
events.where: Biltmore Room, near Track 42 · Grand Central Terminal
events.cost: Browse the public terminal; food and other purchases cost extra.
events.what: Meet Grand Central food vendors at this one-day Thanksgiving market and pick up seasonal provisions in the Biltmore Room. Browsing and buying are separate: allow a budget for any food you choose to take home.
events.imageAlt: The Grand Central Market interior, with its illuminated ceiling decoration.

events.title: Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio
events.when: October 25, 2026–February 27, 2027. Closed Thanksgiving, November 26, and Christmas. Open 10:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; Fridays until 8:30 p.m.
events.where: MoMA · 11 West 53rd Street, sixth floor
events.cost: $30 adults; $22 seniors; $17 full-time students with ID. Special exhibitions included. Free Friday evenings for New York State residents require advance reservations.
events.what: Rarely lent sculptures from the Centre Pompidou join photographs, films, furniture and tools from Brancusi’s Paris studio. The sixth-floor exhibition explores how he arranged works as an environment for living and making.
events.imageAlt: Constantin Brancusi seated among sculptures in his Paris studio, circa 1934; self-portrait supplied by MoMA.
events.imageCredit: Constantin Brancusi. Self-portrait in the studio with Endless Columns I–IV, Fish (1930), Leda (1926). c. 1934. PH 854. Centre Pompidou, Paris. Digital image © CNAC/MNAM, Dist. RMN-Grand Palais / Art Resource, NY. © Succession Brancusi – All rights reserved (Adagp) 2026.

events.title: Gen’ichirō Inokuma’s New York art circle
events.what: Paintings, photographs, film and letters trace Inokuma’s 20 years in New York and friendships across the city’s postwar art world. An indoor exhibition that connects art with the story of a creative neighborhood.
events.where: Japan Society · 333 East 47th Street
events.when: October 6, 2026–January 10, 2027. Tuesday–Friday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; Saturday–Sunday noon–6 p.m.; closed Mondays and major holidays. Check holiday closures before travelling.
events.cost: $20 nonmembers; $15 students/seniors. Free First Friday evenings are limited windows, next listed December 4, 5–7 p.m.; regular gallery admission is paid.
events.imageAlt: Gen’ichirō Inokuma in his 95th Street studio in 1960; photograph courtesy of MIMOCA

events.title: Paper Cuts: a world of zines and independent publishing
events.what: Explore independent publishing through a selection drawn from more than 600 zines and small-press works, with reading tables and a large visual installation. A quiet, creative alternative to a large museum.
events.where: Center for Book Arts · 28 West 27th Street, third floor
events.when: September 10–December 12, 2026. Regular hours Monday–Thursday 11 a.m.–6 p.m., Friday–Saturday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Sunday. Confirm holiday exceptions before travelling.
events.cost: Free exhibition admission; no book purchase required.
events.imageAlt: Zines from the first year of Paper Cuts; photo courtesy of Christopher Kardambikis

events.title: MoMA’s Contenders film season
events.what: MoMA’s annual film selection pairs recent releases with filmmaker conversations at selected screenings. Public tickets normally release one week before each screening at 10:30 a.m. ET. The photograph is an Obsession still used for the season; that opening screening has passed.
events.where: Museum of Modern Art · 11 West 53rd Street
events.when: October 28–December 17, 2026; screening dates and times vary. No Thanksgiving screenings. Upcoming: November 27, Wildwood at 2 p.m. and Bouchra at 5 p.m.
events.cost: $14 adult film ticket, plus $2 for advance online reservations; $12 seniors, $10 students. A screening ticket is required and availability is limited.
events.imageAlt: An Obsession film still showing a man on the telephone in a dim restaurant; courtesy Focus Features via MoMA.
events.imageCredit: Obsession. 2026. USA. Directed by Curry Barker. Courtesy Focus Features.

events.title: Textiles become sculptures in In Fragments
events.what: Blanchard assembles collected cloth, clothing and Mylar into textile trees, vessels and expansive wall pieces. The show brings texture, repair and material memory into sculptural form; plan for an open day after the November holiday closure.
events.where: Jane Lombard Gallery · 58 White Street
events.when: October 30–December 12, 2026. Closed November 25–30; reopens December 1. Regular hours Tuesday–Friday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Saturday, 11 a.m.–6 p.m.
events.cost: No admission charge or required purchase listed by the gallery; artwork purchases are optional.
events.imageAlt: Four long, colorful hanging textile sculptures by Elodie Blanchard displayed on a white gallery wall at Jane Lombard Gallery.

events.title: Yoshitomo Nara’s new paintings and giant heads
events.where: David Zwirner · 537 West 20th Street and 533 West 19th Street
events.when: Nov 5–Dec 12 · check gallery opening hours before visiting
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: A major New York solo presentation brings together paintings, drawings and sculptures. The 19th Street gallery holds thirteen enlarged bronze heads; the 20th Street space focuses on paintings and related works.
events.imageAlt: Artwork from Yoshitomo Nara’s exhibition, courtesy of David Zwirner

events.title: Light sculptures that bend like ribbons
events.where: Museum of Arts and Design · 2 Columbus Circle
events.when: October 27, 2026–April 4, 2027. Closed Thanksgiving, November 26, and Mondays. Wednesday noon–8 p.m.; other open days 10 a.m.–6 p.m.
events.cost: $20 general admission; $16 seniors; $14 students. Pay what you wish only on first Wednesdays, 5–8 p.m., in person.
events.what: Hand-bent ash and embedded LEDs turn into looping light sculptures, sconces and sculptural seating. More than fifteen works shift as you move around them, making this an absorbing indoor design visit after the Thanksgiving closure.
events.imageAlt: Illuminated bentwood loops and curved seating installed in John Procario: Freeforms at the Museum of Arts and Design.

events.title: Chinatown’s neighborhood holiday market
events.when: Next listed weekend November 27–29; season through December 24. Weekly hours: Thursday/Sunday noon–6 p.m., Friday/Saturday noon–8 p.m.; confirm holiday exceptions.
events.where: Welcome to Chinatown Hub · 115 Bowery
events.cost: Free entry; gifts, food and drinks priced separately.
events.what: Browse more than 50 AAPI small-business brands at the indoor Innovation Hub. Thanksgiving weekend features Favor Coffee; later weekends rotate food pop-ups. The organizer says visitors can walk in without an RSVP. Gifts, food and drink are separate purchases.
events.imageAlt: Miniature objects, jewelry and small handmade goods displayed at Welcome to Chinatown’s market.

events.title: Winter Lantern Festival at Snug Harbor
events.when: Selected evenings through January 10; next listed dates November 27–29, 5–10 p.m.; last entry 9 p.m.
events.where: Snug Harbor · 1000 Richmond Terrace
events.cost: Tickets from $18; check date-specific price and checkout fees. Food and travel extra.
events.what: Handmade illuminated Chinese lanterns and an included acrobatic show fill Snug Harbor after dark. Enter at Cottage Row and Chapel Road. Choose a listed operating date; the venue advertises rain-or-shine operation with rescheduling if extreme weather forces closure.
events.imageAlt: The historic buildings and grounds at Snug Harbor, the festival’s host venue; a daytime venue view, not the lantern display.

events.title: Free guided tours of MoMI LAB
events.where: 36-01 35th Avenue
events.when: December 3, 10 and 17 at 5 p.m.; advance RSVP required.
events.cost: Free with RSVP; limited to 15 participants.
events.what: Join a free educator-led visit to MoMI LAB in a group capped at 15 participants. Choose a listed Thursday on the museum’s own reservation form. This is a scheduled lab tour, not a general museum-admission ticket.
events.imageAlt: The Museum of the Moving Image exterior photographed by Marley White; venue photograph.

events.title: Julie Curtiss’s dreamlike New York
events.where: 541 West 24th Street
events.when: Through Dec 19; Tue–Sat, 10 am–6 pm
events.cost: Free gallery admission
events.what: UNREAL turns apartments, bodegas, laundromats and street encounters into unsettling, sharply observed paintings. A compact gallery stop with sly humor and plenty of New York details.
events.imageAlt: Installation photograph of Julie Curtiss’s UNREAL at Gagosian, by Owen Conway.

events.title: Small paintings for a quiet gallery afternoon
events.where: 54 White Street
events.when: Through Jan 9; Tue–Sat, 11 am–6 pm
events.cost: Free gallery admission
events.what: Gareth Cadwallader’s Goodnight Moon brings together intimate watercolors about family, nighttime and the passage of time. The small scale rewards a slow look rather than a quick pass.
events.imageAlt: Installation view of Gareth Cadwallader’s Goodnight Moon at GRIMM.

events.title: Eunnam Hong’s cinematic interiors
events.where: 47 Walker Street
events.when: Nov 11–Jan 9; check gallery hours before visiting
events.cost: Free gallery admission
events.what: The new exhibition 成長物 성장물 uses staged, story-like scenes to explore identity and interior life. A compact gallery stop to pair with a walk through Tribeca.
events.imageAlt: An artwork photographed for Eunnam Hong’s exhibition at Mendes Wood DM.

events.title: Krasner and Pollock, side by side
events.where: 1000 Fifth Avenue, Gallery 899
events.when: October 4, 2026–January 31, 2027. Closed Wednesdays and Thanksgiving, November 26; check current museum hours before travelling.
events.cost: Included with museum admission: general adult $30; seniors $22; students $17. NY State residents and NY/NJ/CT students may pay what they wish, with a $0.01 minimum and eligibility verification.
events.what: More than 120 works trace Lee Krasner’s and Jackson Pollock’s careers together, giving each artist room beyond the usual shorthand. Allow time for the exhibition and bring accepted proof for resident admission.
events.imageAlt: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, in the museum’s visitor photograph.

events.title: Holiday lights under 44 glowing stars
events.where: 10 Columbus Circle
events.when: Nov 9–Jan 3; light shows every 30 minutes, 5 pm–midnight
events.cost: Free to view; shopping and dining optional
events.what: Look up through the Great Room at 44 illuminated stars and a light-and-music show every half hour from 5 p.m. to midnight. Free Broadway performances are scheduled December 3, 10 and 17, 5–6 p.m. Shopping and dining are optional.
events.imageAlt: The glass exterior of the Shops at Columbus Circle with illuminated purple stars visible inside.

events.title: A British holiday panto on the Lower East Side
events.where: 317 East Houston Street
events.when: Selected dates through December 20; next shows November 27 at 5 p.m. and November 28 at 4 p.m.; doors 30 minutes earlier.
events.cost: General admission $40 plus sales tax and a $3.78 booking fee. Reserved seating $50 plus tax and fee.
events.what: An adults-only British-style Peter Pan panto mixes pop-song parodies, original music, drag, satire and audience participation in Parkside Lounge’s back room. Ages 21+ with physical photo ID; flashing lights and fog may be used. Choose a listed performance; early-bird tickets have ended.
events.imageAlt: Parkside Lounge’s back-room performance space; venue photograph.

events.title: The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade
events.where: Central Park West to Herald Square; designated viewing areas
events.when: Nov 26, Thanksgiving morning; verify the final public-viewing map
events.cost: Free public street viewing; reserved experiences are separate
events.what: The centennial parade plans a record 100 inflatable elements, alongside floats, performers and the traditional Santa finale. Expect crowds, arrive early and consult the official route and access restrictions before leaving.
events.imageAlt: Macy’s courtesy photograph of a previous Thanksgiving Day Parade; not the 2026 event.

events.title: A guided look at Wave Hill’s autumn garden
events.where: Meet at Perkins Visitor Center, 4900 Independence Avenue
events.when: Remaining walk November 29, 1–1:45 p.m.; drop in at Perkins Visitor Center.
events.cost: $10 adult grounds admission; the walk is included
events.what: Join a garden interpreter for the final listed fall highlights walk. It is included with grounds admission; no registration is required. Paths vary in surface and slope, with an accessible route available on request. Severe weather cancels the walk.
events.imageAlt: Autumn garden plantings and broad banana leaves at Wave Hill; official garden photograph.

events.title: A Christmas Carol in a candlelit historic parlor
events.when: Selected performances Nov 24–Jan 3; 70 minutes
events.cost: $50–$130; optional reception costs $35 extra
events.where: Merchant’s House Museum · 29 E 4th Street
events.what: John Kevin Jones and Vince Gatton alternate as Dickens in a solo telling drawn from his own script. The small 1832 house’s double parlor supplies the setting. Doors open 30 minutes before the performance; check the exact performance when booking.
events.imageAlt: John Kevin Jones and Vince Gatton in the producer’s cast photograph

events.title: A Christmas Carol at PAC NYC
events.when: Previews begin Nov 20; runs through Jan 3
events.cost: Paid tickets; current price depends on seat and performance
events.where: Perelman Performing Arts Center · 251 Fulton Street
events.what: Jack Thorne and Matthew Warchus’s adaptation returns with Andy Karl as Scrooge. The audience surrounds the action in this carol-filled production. Select a specific performance before making plans. The photograph shows an earlier PAC NYC staging.
events.imageAlt: Actors in an earlier PAC NYC staging of A Christmas Carol

events.title: Blue Man Group: A New Holiday Surprise
events.when: Nov 12–Jan 3; performance times vary
events.cost: Broadway Direct currently lists $59–$295 including fees; actual price varies by performance and seat.
events.where: Lunt-Fontanne Theatre · 205 W 46th Street
events.what: The group’s first Broadway holiday production combines percussion, visual comedy and seasonal surprises. Check the official ticket calendar for your preferred date; the production is largely non-verbal.
events.imageAlt: A Blue Man Group performer in the official show photograph

events.title: New York City Ballet’s The Nutcracker
events.when: Regular performances November 27–January 2; separate sensory-friendly performance January 3 at 1 p.m.
events.cost: Paid tickets plus required fees; seat/date pricing varies
events.where: David H. Koch Theater · 20 Lincoln Center Plaza
events.what: New York City Ballet performs Balanchine’s holiday classic with Tschaikovsky’s score, a growing Christmas tree and the company’s full stage production. Allow about two hours. The January 3 performance has adjustments to lighting and sound for guests with sensory processing needs; select the intended performance when booking.
events.imageAlt: A scene from New York City Ballet’s The Nutcracker

events.title: Big Apple Circus returns under the big top
events.when: Nov 27–Jan 18; 2 hours 10 minutes including intermission
events.cost: Tickets from $41.87 including taxes and fees on the official Eventim booking page; prices vary by date and seat.
events.where: Marx Brothers Playground · E 96th Street between First and Second Avenues
events.what: The circus moves east while Lincoln Center is renovated. The new show includes the Cardenas Brothers and Sky Angels, with aerial acts, acrobatics and comedy. Check the new location when arranging travel.
events.imageAlt: The Cardenas Brothers in an official Big Apple Circus photograph

events.title: Holiday Express: vintage toys and trains
events.source: The New York Historical / NYC Tourism + Conventions
events.when: Nov 13–Mar 14; museum opening hours apply
events.cost: Included with paid museum admission; check current ticket prices
events.where: The New York Historical · 170 Central Park West
events.what: Historic toy trains, stations and miniature buildings return in the annual Jerni Collection display. The objects trace changing designs from the early twentieth century through World War II. The museum-supplied photo shows an earlier display.
events.imageAlt: An earlier Holiday Express miniature train display; photo credited to the New York Historical Society

events.title: The Met’s Christmas tree and Neapolitan crèche
events.when: Nov 24–Jan 6; check museum closures before visiting
events.cost: Included with museum admission; eligible NY residents pay what they wish
events.where: The Met Fifth Avenue · Gallery 305
events.what: The annual tree and eighteenth-century Neapolitan nativity figures fill the Medieval Sculpture Hall. Make it a focused holiday gallery visit; the museum is closed Wednesdays and Thanksgiving, so the listed exhibition end does not imply public access that day.
events.imageAlt: The Met’s decorated Christmas tree and nativity display

events.title: Downtown Brooklyn Gets Lit!
events.when: Tue Nov 24 · 6–7 p.m.
events.cost: Free admission; purchases and transport optional
events.where: Albee Square
events.what: Join the neighborhood’s holiday-light countdown, with DJ Mike, light performances, juggling and stilt walking. The organizer also lists hot chocolate and a Grinch photo opportunity. Dress for an outdoor evening.
events.imageAlt: A previous Downtown Brooklyn holiday-lighting celebration

events.title: Now You See Me Live on Broadway
events.when: Through January 3; next official performances November 27 at 3 p.m. and 7:30 p.m.; 90 minutes without intermission.
events.cost: Full-price tickets $50.40–$290.08 as listed by TDF. Official box-office rush $42 including fees, subject to availability; limit two per person.
events.where: Al Hirschfeld Theatre · 302 W 45th Street
events.what: Four illusionists—Gabriella Lester, James More, Darcy Oake and Matthew Pomeroy—bring escape acts, visual illusions and solo stunts to Broadway. Ages 5+; the production uses strobes, lasers, loud effects and theatrical haze. Select an actual performance on the official calendar.
events.imageAlt: Broadway cast member Gabriella Lester in an official production portrait

events.title: Shuling Guo: Temple II
events.when: October 15–December 5, 2026. Closed November 26–27; reopens Saturday, November 28 at 11 a.m. Regular hours Tuesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.
events.cost: No admission charge or required purchase listed by the gallery; artwork purchases are optional.
events.where: Hollis Taggart Downtown · 109 Norfolk Street
events.what: New paintings and a site-specific mural connect botanical forms, the female body and devotional imagery with motherhood, memory and loss. This intimate Lower East Side show returns after its Thanksgiving closure on November 28.
events.imageAlt: A Shuling Guo painting with pale birds and botanical forms against a deep blue and gold background, photographed for Temple II.

events.title: Teruko Yokoi: Seasons
events.when: Through Nov 25; check gallery visiting hours
events.cost: Free gallery admission
events.where: Hollis Taggart · 521 W 26th Street, first floor
events.what: Explore Yokoi’s paintings at the gallery’s Chelsea space. This is a separate exhibition from the downtown Shuling Guo show, offering another perspective on abstraction and the natural world.
events.imageAlt: Teruko Yokoi painting photographed for the Seasons exhibition

events.title: Bacon / de Kooning in an Upper East Side townhouse
events.when: Through Dec 19; check gallery visiting hours
events.cost: Free gallery admission
events.where: Lévy Gorvy Dayan · 19 E 64th Street
events.what: The exhibition places the artists’ smaller-scale paintings from the late 1960s and 1970s in conversation. It focuses on their shared use of paint to express the human figure, while making their very different approaches visible.
events.imageAlt: A framed painting photographed for the Bacon / de Kooning exhibition

events.title: Holiday tree lighting at the Seaport
events.where: Fulton & Front Streets
events.when: Dec 1 · exact program time not yet listed
events.cost: Free outdoor event.
events.what: The Seaport’s annual tree-lighting celebration returns to its cobblestone streets. The organizer confirms December 1; check the event page for the final program and arrival time.
events.imageAlt: Santa beside a pianist during a previous Seaport holiday celebration; organizer photograph.

events.title: A visit to Macy’s Santaland
events.where: Macy’s Herald Square · 8th floor · 151 W. 34th Street
events.when: Nov 27–Dec 24 · reserved arrival times
events.cost: Standard visit free; reservation required. Optional premium experiences cost extra.
events.what: Walk through the holiday village and visit Santa. Standard reservations open November 20 on a rolling seven-day schedule. This is a ticketed reservation visit even though standard admission is free; confirm an available slot before going.
events.imageAlt: Macy’s Herald Square exterior, photographed by Laura Miller for NYC Tourism; a venue photograph, not this year’s Santaland.

events.title: PaleyLand holiday screenings and displays
events.where: 25 W. 52nd Street
events.when: Nov 28–Jan 10 · Wednesday–Sunday, noon–6 p.m.
events.cost: Adult general admission $20; Santa visits +$15 and gaming +$10.
events.what: Holiday television screenings, character appearances, crafts, hot chocolate and a model-train display fill the museum. Santa visits and gaming are optional paid additions. Open Monday–Thursday of Christmas week; closes at 4 p.m. on December 24 and 31. Check the character calendar before booking.
events.imageAlt: An audience seated in the Paley Museum’s Bennack Theater; official venue photograph.

events.title: Cheer on the Prospect Park Turkey Trot
events.where: Prospect Park · Center Drive start; Harry’s Wall finish
events.when: Nov 26 · waves at 8:15 and 9 a.m.; finish area closes 10:40 a.m.
events.cost: Free to spectate from public paths; runner registration is sold out.
events.what: Bundle up for Thanksgiving-morning cheering along the five-mile race. This suggestion is for spectators: no race bibs remain. Keep the course clear and use the organizer’s route map to choose a public viewing spot.
events.imageAlt: An archival Turkey Trot race photograph published by Prospect Park Track Club, with a participant pushing a wheelchair along the course.

events.title: Post-Thanksgiving woodland hike at High Rock
events.where: Nevada Avenue Parking Lot · 200 Nevada Avenue
events.when: Nov 27 · 10 a.m.–noon
events.cost: Free; registration not required.
events.what: Join the Rangers for a two-hour loop through High Rock’s woodland trails. The route has uphill and downhill sections; boots or sneakers are required. Bring water and layers, and allow time for travel to Staten Island.
events.imageAlt: A pond surrounded by trees in NYC Parks’ archival photograph of High Rock Park.

events.title: Holiday lights and movie-sites bus tour
events.where: Departure near Broadway & W. 63rd Street; booking supplies exact meeting point
events.when: Nov 25–Jan 2 season · select departures; about three hours
events.cost: Adult tickets from $78; premium seating from $82.
events.what: A guided bus ride connects holiday displays with New York film locations. Confirm the departure calendar before booking. Displays change through the season; the Rockefeller tree is not lit before its December ceremony.
events.imageAlt: Visitors by a decorated shop window in On Location Tours’ archival holiday-tour photograph.

events.title: RAINS sample sale
events.where: 468 Broadway
events.cost: Merchandise priced individually; item prices are not published.
events.what: Browse RAINS outerwear and accessories at the Broadway sale. The detailed organizer page gives the November 18–25 schedule. Availability and sizes vary; check the sale terms before purchasing.
events.imageAlt: A model wearing RAINS outerwear in the organizer’s official sale photograph.

events.title: John Elliott sample sale
events.where: 468 Broadway
events.cost: Merchandise priced individually; item prices are not published.
events.what: The John Elliott sale runs at 260’s Broadway location. Browse the available clothing selection; stock, sizing and final-sale terms should be checked on site.
events.imageAlt: A model in a John Elliott jacket in the organizer’s official sale photograph.

events.title: Georg Baselitz: Meine Schule
events.where: 555 W. 24th Street
events.when: Nov 12–Jan 23 · Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: See Baselitz’s latest exhibition at the Chelsea gallery. A focused indoor art stop; check holiday closures before making the trip.
events.imageAlt: An installation photograph from Georg Baselitz’s Meine Schule exhibition, courtesy Gagosian.

events.title: Friends & Legends: Michael Chow’s collection
events.where: 980 Madison Avenue · entrance at 974 Madison
events.when: Nov 14–Dec 22 · Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–7 p.m.
events.cost: Free gallery admission.
events.what: A portrait-focused selection from Michael Chow’s collection brings together artists including Basquiat, Warhol, Haring and Hockney. Check holiday hours before visiting the Madison Avenue gallery.
events.imageAlt: Portraits and sculpture installed in Friends & Legends, photographed for Gagosian.

events.title: Fantasy and Reality: The Art of Johan Tobias Sergel
events.where: The Morgan Library & Museum · 225 Madison Avenue
events.when: Oct 30–Jan 31 · Tue–Sun; closed Mondays and Thanksgiving. Fridays until 8 p.m.
events.cost: Adults $25; online service fees apply. Free Fridays 5–8 p.m. require reservations.
events.what: Drawings and sculptures in marble, bronze, terracotta and plaster trace the Swedish artist’s working process. The exhibition pairs finished works with models and imaginative studies, including his celebrated Faun.
events.imageAlt: Johan Tobias Sergel’s drawn study of Diomedes’ helmet and head in profile, circa 1771; photograph by Cecilia Heisser, Nationalmuseum.

events.title: FAD’s holiday makers market at Empire Stores
events.where: Empire Stores · 55 Water Street
events.when: Nov 30–Dec 20 · daily 11 a.m.–6 p.m.
events.cost: Free admission; shopping optional.
events.what: Browse handcrafted jewelry, clothing, homewares and small gifts inside the waterfront warehouse. More than 35 makers join on weekends, with smaller weekday markets of 14 makers.
events.imageAlt: An earlier FAD makers market inside Empire Stores, photographed for the organizer.

events.title: Bryant Park Tree Lighting
events.what: A free holiday show pairs figure-skating performances with choir music and the lighting of Bryant Park’s tree. Entry begins at 3:30 p.m. and is first come, first served; capacity is limited and there is no re-entry once full.
events.where: Bryant Park · rink deck, between Fifth and Sixth Avenues at 40th–42nd Streets
events.when: December 1, 5:30–6:30 p.m.; entry from 3:30 p.m.
events.cost: Free viewing. Food and skating afterward cost extra; skating is a separate reservation.
events.imageAlt: Skaters performing beneath Bryant Park’s illuminated tree at the 2024 lighting; organizer photograph by Ryan Muir.

events.title: Columbus Circle Holiday Market
events.what: Browse artisan gifts, jewelry, home goods and seasonal food at the southwest corner of Central Park. It is an easy stop to pair with a park stroll; purchases are optional.
events.where: Columbus Circle · Central Park’s southwest entrance at 59th Street
events.when: December 1–31; Monday–Thursday 11 a.m.–7 p.m., Friday–Sunday 10 a.m.–8 p.m.
events.cost: Free to browse; all shopping and food purchases are optional.
events.imageAlt: Snow-covered market stalls around the Maine Monument at Columbus Circle, in an organizer photograph from an earlier season.

events.title: Sip & Craft Wreathmaking at Wave Hill
events.what: Make a natural wreath with freshly harvested greens and instruction from designer Hanako Shimamoto. Materials and one mulled wine or hot cocoa are included; adults 21+ only and advance registration is encouraged.
events.where: Wave Hill · Armor Hall, 4900 Independence Avenue, Bronx
events.when: December 5, 5–6:30 p.m.
events.cost: $85 including garden admission, materials and one drink; members save 10%. Additional food and drinks extra.
events.imageAlt: Two people assembling natural wreaths at Wave Hill; organizer photograph by Erica Berger.

events.title: Holidays at the Park
events.what: A weekend market of independent artists, makers and small businesses in Bella Abzug Park, with optional food and gift shopping. The next market is November 28 after the November 22 weather cancellation.
events.where: Bella Abzug Park · 524 West 34th Street
events.when: Next market November 28–29, 1–5 p.m.; subsequent Saturdays and Sundays through December 13 generally noon–5 p.m. Check day-specific weather updates.
events.cost: Free admission; food, drinks and shopping optional and extra.
events.imageAlt: Two vendors behind a table of chocolate products at an earlier Holidays at the Park market.

events.title: A Rock’n Holiday Spectacular
events.what: A holiday concert with Jay & The Americans, The Brooklyn Bridge, Ronn David McPhatter’s Drifters, Bobby Wilson, The Chiclettes and Vinnie Medugno, backed by The Coda Band.
events.where: St. George Theatre · 35 Hyatt Street, Staten Island
events.when: December 4, 7:30 p.m.; doors 6:30 p.m.
events.cost: $49–$89 listed by the theatre; confirm final checkout total.
events.imageAlt: Ornate balcony and stage inside St. George Theatre; official venue photograph.

events.title: Madison Square Park Holiday Festival
events.what: A neighborhood festival with live music, warm drinks and seasonal treats, ending with the lighting of a 40-foot Norway spruce. Giveaways are first come, first served while supplies last; the tree area will be crowded.
events.where: Madison Square Park · South Gravel and Northern Reflecting Pool
events.when: December 3, noon–5:30 p.m.; tree lighting at 5 p.m. by the Northern Reflecting Pool.
events.cost: Free; reservations optional for event updates.
events.imageAlt: Green lawns and trees in Madison Square Park with the Flatiron Building beyond; an official park photograph, not the holiday festival.

events.title: Central Park Holiday Lighting
events.what: Sing carols on the plaza, warm up with cocoa and watch a flotilla of illuminated trees on the Harlem Meer. The celebration goes ahead rain, snow or shine; organized groups are not permitted.
events.where: Charles A. Dana Discovery Center · East 110th Street, Central Park
events.when: December 3, 5:30 p.m.
events.cost: Free community holiday celebration.
events.imageAlt: Illuminated trees floating on the Harlem Meer beside the Dana Discovery Center at an earlier holiday lighting.

events.title: Herald Holiday Fair: carousel and winter rides
events.what: Take a spin on the illuminated double-decker Christmas Carousel or try the snow slide in Greeley Square. Tickets are sold onsite; outdoor rides close in bad weather.
events.where: Greeley Square · Broadway at 32nd–33rd Streets
events.when: Daily 10 a.m.–10 p.m. through January 2; closed Thanksgiving Day.
events.cost: Carousel $10 per person; snow slide $7 for one ride or $15 for three rides; VR sleigh $10. Tickets onsite.
events.imageAlt: The illuminated double-decker Christmas Carousel beside Herald Square in a 2025 organizer photograph.

events.title: DUMBO Shop the Studios
events.what: Meet artists and browse original handmade work in 85 participating studios and galleries. Pick up a printed map at 20 Jay Street, 45 Main Street, 55 Washington Street or the Dumbo Flea; purchases are optional.
events.where: Participating DUMBO studios; maps at 20 Jay Street and other listed lobbies
events.when: December 5, noon–6 p.m.
events.cost: Free entry; no RSVP required. Art purchases optional.
events.imageAlt: Visitors walking along a DUMBO street toward the Brooklyn Bridge in an Art in DUMBO neighborhood photograph.

events.title: Winter Wonder at Queens Botanical Garden
events.what: Live music, seasonal crafts, evergreen displays and festive shopping accompany lantern-making from 2–4:30 p.m. The tree-lighting ceremony runs 4:35–5 p.m.; food, drinks and shop purchases are optional extras.
events.where: Queens Botanical Garden · 43-50 Main Street
events.when: December 6, 2–5 p.m.
events.cost: $6 nonmember adult admission, including garden entry; members free. Food, drink and shopping extra.
events.imageAlt: A pink ornament on an evergreen at Queens Botanical Garden during Winter Wonder 2023; photograph by E. Hatzithomas.

events.title: Wave Hill Artisan Market
events.when: December 5, 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; December 6, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.
events.where: Wave Hill House and Glyndor Gallery · 4900 Independence Avenue, Bronx
events.cost: Included with $10 adult garden admission; members free. Shopping and food extra.
events.what: Meet local makers across Wave Hill House and Glyndor Gallery, with dozens of vendors selling handmade gifts. The market runs later than regular garden hours on Saturday; Sunday ends at 4 p.m.
events.imageAlt: Visitors browsing a vendor’s table decorated with evergreen garlands at an earlier Wave Hill Artisan Market; photograph by Erica Berger.

events.title: FIELD + SUPPLY Holiday MRKT
events.when: December 5–6, 10 a.m.–5 p.m. both days.
events.where: Starrett-Lehigh Building · 601 West 26th Street, fourth floor
events.cost: Early-bird admission through December 4: $20 one day or $30 both days; afterward $25 or $35. Under 12 free. Shopping and selected workshops or portraits extra.
events.what: An indoor holiday market of ceramics, jewelry, clothing, home goods and pantry gifts from independent makers. Drop-in olive oil tastings and fragrance-layering sessions join the shopping; portrait sessions and some workshops have separate fees. Rain or shine.
events.imageAlt: Shoppers and vendor displays inside an earlier market at the Starrett-Lehigh Building; official venue photograph.

events.where: New Museum · 235 Bowery
events.cost: $28 adult admission. Thursday 7–9 p.m. is pay-what-you-wish with advance reservation; this does not make regular admission free.
events.title: The Bowery: Devil’s Mile
events.when: September 25–January 18. Tuesday–Sunday 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; Thursday until 9 p.m. Closed Mondays and Thanksgiving.
events.what: Trace the Bowery’s changing life from a Lenape footpath and entertainment district to an artists’ neighborhood. The exhibition follows the people and places behind the street’s reinventions, including figures such as Jacob Riis, Eva Hesse and Keith Haring.
events.imageAlt: A black-and-white 1945 Weegee photograph of a performer in a winged devil costume, presented by the New Museum; © Weegee / International Center of Photography.

events.where: New Museum · 235 Bowery
events.cost: $28 adult admission. Thursday 7–9 p.m. is pay-what-you-wish with advance reservation; this does not make regular admission free.
events.title: Ho Tzu Nyen: P for Power — Up Down
events.when: September 25–January 25. Tuesday–Sunday 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; Thursday until 9 p.m. Closed Mondays and Thanksgiving.
events.what: An unusual video commission occupies the museum’s glass-front elevators. Digitally rendered children deliver riddles and reflections about political and technological power, endurance and personal agency. Encounter the work as part of a museum visit; it is a compact installation rather than a gallery survey.
events.imageAlt: The New Museum’s two adjoining buildings on the Bowery at dusk, with pedestrians crossing in front; photograph by Jason O’Rear.

events.title: Na Mira: NO SMOKING
events.what: Infrared videos, holographic projections and a moving soundscape turn MoMA’s Studio into an installation about how imaging technologies shape perception. The card photograph is the artist’s work-in-progress view, not the completed installation.
events.where: MoMA · 11 West 53rd Street · Floor 4, Kravis Studio
events.when: November 14–February 15. Daily 10:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; Fridays until 8:30 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.
events.cost: $30 adult admission, including special exhibitions. New York State residents can reserve free Friday tickets for 5:30–8:30 p.m.
events.imageAlt: A wheeled black monitor in a sunlit studio in Na Mira’s 2026 work-in-progress photograph for NO SMOKING; courtesy the artist.

events.title: Kent Monkman: Officer and Laughing Girl
events.what: New paintings respond to Vermeer’s Officer and Laughing Girl through Indigenous perspectives on trade, colonization and cultural encounters. After the Cabinet Gallery installation, see the Vermeer that prompted it in the permanent collection.
events.where: The Frick Collection · 1 East 70th Street · Cabinet Gallery
events.when: November 12–February 22. Wednesday–Monday 10:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; closed Tuesdays and Thanksgiving.
events.cost: $30 adults; advance timed tickets are recommended. Wednesday 1:30–5:30 p.m. is pay what you wish: online tickets have a $5 minimum and guarantee entry, while smaller contributions are available in person subject to capacity.
events.imageAlt: The Frick Collection’s limestone facade and formal garden; official venue photograph.

events.title: Sculpting Sound: Günther Kieser’s Music Posters
events.what: Explore concert posters whose surprising images began as physical models and collages, tracing Günther Kieser’s work from jazz to rock. Allow about 20 minutes for this focused lower-level exhibition; museum admission also covers the other galleries.
events.where: Poster House · 119 West 23rd Street · Lower Level Hallways
events.when: November 12–April 11. Thursday, Saturday and Sunday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Friday 10 a.m.–9 p.m. Closed Monday–Wednesday and Thanksgiving.
events.cost: $15 adults; free admission every Friday and on the third Sunday of each month.
events.imageAlt: Poster House’s illuminated 23rd Street storefront at dusk, with visitors on the sidewalk; official venue photograph.

events.title: Rembrandt’s Lions: Art and Exile in the Dutch Republic
events.what: Drawings, prints and paintings explore the migrants, exiles and refugees who shaped Rembrandt’s Amsterdam. Rarely exhibited Morgan etchings appear alongside loans, with the lion as a recurring symbol of the Dutch Republic.
events.where: The Morgan Library & Museum · 225 Madison Avenue at 36th Street
events.when: October 23–January 31. Tuesday–Sunday 10:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; Friday until 8 p.m. Closed Mondays and Thanksgiving.
events.cost: $25 adults; online service fees apply. Friday 5–8 p.m. is free with a required reservation, released one week ahead.
events.source: The Morgan Library & Museum / NYC Tourism
events.imageAlt: The Morgan Library’s stone portico and lioness sculptures seen from its garden; venue photograph courtesy the Morgan Library.

events.title: Architects of Liberation: Modernism in Western Africa
events.what: About 450 drawings, models, photographs and other objects explore how newly independent nations used modern architecture to imagine their futures. The exhibition spans seven West African countries and connects city planning, housing and education to political independence.
events.where: MoMA · 11 West 53rd Street · Floor 3, Menschel Galleries
events.when: July 5–January 2. Daily 10:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; Fridays until 8:30 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.
events.cost: $30 adult admission, including special exhibitions. New York State residents may reserve free Friday tickets for 5:30–8:30 p.m.
events.imageAlt: Michel Fegyveres’s photograph of the geometric Centre International du Commerce Extérieur du Sénégal in Dakar, shown by MoMA for Architects of Liberation.

events.where: Museum of Arts and Design · 2 Columbus Circle
events.cost: $20 general admission. Pay what you wish only on the first Wednesday of the month, 5–8 p.m., with tickets obtained in person; regular admission is paid.
events.title: Nike: Form Follows Motion
events.when: September 12–March 7. Tuesday and Thursday–Sunday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Wednesday noon–8 p.m. Closed Mondays and Thanksgiving, November 26.
events.what: Follow five decades of footwear and sportswear design through rare Nike prototypes, original design studies and collaborations. The museum installation includes archival shoes and athletic clothing, while the Soles of New York audio guide adds stories from local athletes, designers and sneaker fans.
events.imageAlt: Sportswear on suspended mannequins and shoes in blue-lit display cases inside Nike: Form Follows Motion at the Museum of Arts and Design.

events.where: Museum of Arts and Design · 2 Columbus Circle
events.cost: $20 general admission. Pay what you wish only on the first Wednesday of the month, 5–8 p.m., with tickets obtained in person; regular admission is paid.
events.title: Alice Riehl’s Porcelain Florilegium
events.when: February 28–April 4. Tuesday and Thursday–Sunday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Wednesday noon–8 p.m. Closed Mondays and Thanksgiving, November 26.
events.what: Look closely at monumental porcelain wall murals shaped into branches, flowers and textured botanical forms. Riehl draws on French tapestries, decorative arts and the plants that persist in city environments. The current presentation has reopened after its October 4–27 installation closure.
events.imageAlt: Botanical porcelain murals across white and dark gallery walls, with drawing tables below, in Alice Riehl’s Porcelain Florilegium at MAD.

events.title: No Ordinary Light: Akari at 75
events.what: Explore Noguchi’s paper-and-bamboo light sculptures alongside works in stone, metal and clay. The exhibition revisits intimate rooms and monumental installations, including ideas from the Eames House and the artist’s 1986 Venice Biennale presentation.
events.where: The Noguchi Museum · 9-01 33rd Road at Vernon Boulevard
events.when: November 4–September 5. Wednesday–Sunday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; last entry 4:30 p.m. Closed Mondays, Tuesdays and Thanksgiving, November 26.
events.cost: $16 general admission. Free on the first Friday of each month; no advance reservations are currently taken, so buy tickets at the museum.
events.imageAlt: Glowing paper Akari light sculptures and stone works in a wood-floored Noguchi Museum gallery; installation photograph by Nicholas Knight.

events.title: Lincoln Square Magical Lights Ceremony
events.when: December 1, starting at 4:30 p.m.
events.where: Dante Park · Broadway and West 64th Street
events.cost: Free outdoor ceremony, performances and complimentary hot chocolate; nearby food and shopping optional and extra.
events.what: Circus acts and the Special Music School Chorus open the holiday-lighting celebration, followed by swing music from Saints of Swing. Enjoy the suspended park lights, hot chocolate, treats and neighborhood festivities; this card is for the December 1 opening ceremony.
events.imageAlt: Holiday performers, including stilt walkers and a unicyclist, pose beneath illuminated trees at an earlier Lincoln Square Magical Lights celebration; official organizer photograph.

events.title: Brooklyn Flea Holiday Market
events.what: Browse vintage clothing, records, jewelry and handmade gifts beneath the Manhattan Bridge, with festive decor and live performances. Drinks from the Archway Bar and vendor purchases cost extra.
events.where: DUMBO Archway and Plaza · 80 Pearl Street
events.when: Remaining Saturdays and Sundays, November 28–December 20, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
events.cost: Free admission; shopping and refreshments optional and extra.
events.imageAlt: Holiday Flea vendors and shoppers beneath the DUMBO Archway in a 2025 photograph by Ming Fai Chan.

events.title: Making Music: Helen Frankenthaler Prints
events.what: A focused installation of nine prints connects Frankenthaler’s abstract color with her love of jazz, ballet and opera. Works from 1965–2000 reveal how music influenced both her titles and her experiments with printmaking.
events.where: Grey Art Museum, NYU · 18 Cooper Square
events.when: September 9, 2026–July 3, 2027. Tue/Thu/Fri 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; Wed to 8 p.m.; Sat to 5 p.m. Closed Sun/Mon. November 25 closes at 6 p.m.; closed November 26–28.
events.cost: Free admission for everyone; optional suggested donation $5.
events.source: Grey Art Museum, New York University
events.imageAlt: Nine colorful abstract prints displayed on a white gallery wall in Making Music at the Grey Art Museum; photograph by Mikhail Mishin.

events.title: FAD Market Holiday Pop-Up in Cobble Hill
events.what: Browse over 70 independent makers, designers and food businesses in St. Paul’s historic hall. Each of the three weekends has a different vendor lineup, with ceramics, jewelry, home goods, clothing and small edible gifts.
events.where: St. Paul · 190 Court Street, Brooklyn
events.when: December 5–6, 12–13 and 19–20, 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; weekends only.
events.cost: Free admission; shopping and food purchases optional.
events.imageAlt: Visitors browsing food, jewelry and art stalls beneath strings of lights at an earlier FAD holiday market in St. Paul’s hall.

events.title: By Alison Knowles: A Retrospective
events.what: More than 200 works trace six decades of Knowles’s experimental art, from Fluxus scores and artist’s books to sculpture, sound and installations. The show explores how everyday materials and simple actions become art.
events.where: Grey Art Museum, NYU · 18 Cooper Square
events.when: September 9, 2026–January 30, 2027. Tue/Thu/Fri 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; Wed to 8 p.m.; Sat to 5 p.m. Closed Sun/Mon. November 25 closes at 6 p.m.; closed November 26–28.
events.cost: Free admission; optional suggested donation $5.
events.imageAlt: A large wooden mixed-media installation with a blue tunnel and cyanotype panels in the Alison Knowles retrospective; photograph by Mikhail Mishin.

events.title: Washington Square Tree Lighting & Caroling
events.what: Sing beneath the arch with the Rob Susman Brass Quartet and singer Linseigh Green as the neighborhood tree is illuminated. The association provides songbooks; donations support this volunteer-run tradition but are optional.
events.where: Washington Square Arch · Fifth Avenue at Washington Square North
events.when: December 8, 2026, from 6 p.m.
events.cost: Free; donations appreciated but never required.
events.imageAlt: A crowd gathered beneath Washington Square Arch around an illuminated Christmas tree at an earlier neighborhood celebration.

events.title: Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Lighting
events.what: The 76-foot Norway spruce is illuminated with more than 50,000 lights during the annual broadcast. The plaza ceremony is reserved for invited guests; public viewing is from surrounding streets on a first-come basis. Expect security checkpoints, street closures and long outdoor waits.
events.where: Rockefeller Center · surrounding streets near 49th–50th Streets and Rockefeller Plaza
events.when: December 2, 2026, 7–10 p.m.; tree lighting near the end of the broadcast.
events.cost: Free public street viewing; no public tickets and no access to the invited-guest plaza ceremony.
events.imageAlt: Rockefeller Center’s illuminated tree above the Prometheus statue and a stage during an earlier televised lighting ceremony.

events.title: I’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers
events.what: Photography, installations and photobooks by 28 artists examine everyday life and women’s roles in Japan from the 1950s onward. Organized with Aperture, this first U.S. presentation brings different generations and approaches into conversation.
events.where: International Center of Photography · 84 Ludlow Street
events.when: October 15, 2026–January 11, 2027. Daily 10:30 a.m.–6:30 p.m.; Thursday until 8 p.m. Last entry 30 minutes before closing. Closed November 26.
events.cost: Adult admission $18; Thursday 5–8 p.m. admission $5. Other discounts apply.
events.imageAlt: Kawauchi Rinko’s close-up photograph of an eye against a blue background, Untitled, 2004, from the eyes, the ears.

events.title: Melissa Ann Pinney: What’s Ms. Pinney Doing Here?
events.what: Pinney’s photographs of Chicago public-school students explore adolescence, identity and community. This focused presentation occupies ICP’s ground-floor Incubator Space, which is free to enter separately from the ticketed galleries.
events.where: International Center of Photography, Incubator Space · 84 Ludlow Street
events.when: October 22, 2026–January 11, 2027, during café and museum hours. Museum daily 10:30 a.m.–6:30 p.m.; Thursday until 8 p.m. Closed November 26.
events.cost: Free admission to the ground-floor Incubator Space; upstairs exhibitions require separate admission.
events.imageAlt: Students gathered around an outdoor school bench in Melissa Ann Pinney’s 2019 photograph at Ogden-Jenner Middle School.

events.title: Sacred Splendor: Ritual Art and Treasures from Prague
events.what: More than 160 objects spanning six centuries bring Jewish ritual art together with Christian treasures from Prague’s St. Vitus Cathedral. Metalwork, manuscripts and ceremonial objects trace connections among artists, materials and communities in Central Europe.
events.where: The Jewish Museum · Fifth Avenue at 92nd Street
events.when: September 18, 2026–February 7, 2027. Sun/Mon 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; Thu until 8 p.m.; Fri until 4 p.m.; Sat until 6 p.m. Closed Tue/Wed and November 26.
events.cost: Adult admission $24; seniors $14; students $10. Free Saturdays and the third Thursday of the month, 5–8 p.m.
events.imageAlt: Museum photographs of an ornate gold-colored Gothic sacrament house and a silver tower-shaped spice container, displayed side by side.

events.title: Hannah Altman: Not a Circle but a Spiral
events.what: A focused photography installation explores Jewish ritual and folklore through everyday objects, gestures and scenes, including newly commissioned work. Presented on the third floor as an artist’s response to Sacred Splendor; it is a distinct focus gallery within the same museum visit.
events.where: The Jewish Museum, Focus Gallery · Fifth Avenue at 92nd Street
events.when: September 18, 2026–February 7, 2027. Sun/Mon 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; Thu until 8 p.m.; Fri until 4 p.m.; Sat until 6 p.m. Closed Tue/Wed and November 26.
events.cost: Included with museum admission: adults $24, seniors $14, students $10. Free admission on Saturdays and the third Thursday, 5–8 p.m.; these are specific free-entry windows.
events.imageAlt: A person with closed eyes blowing a curved shofar in Hannah Altman’s photograph Shofar (To Catch One’s Breath), 2024.

events.title: Murray Hill Holiday Party & Tree Lighting
events.what: A neighborhood evening begins with an outdoor tree lighting on Park Avenue, followed by food, drinks and a community gathering inside the Church of Our Saviour. The celebration marks 144 years since the first electrically lit Christmas tree in Murray Hill.
events.where: Park Avenue at 38th Street, then Church of Our Saviour · 59 Park Avenue
events.when: December 3, 2026, 6–8:30 p.m. Outdoor gathering at 6 p.m.; indoor party 6:30–8:30 p.m.
events.cost: $35 for nonmembers/nonparishioners. Free tickets for MHNA members and Church of Our Saviour parishioners; reserve the appropriate ticket.
events.imageAlt: Carolers wearing red scarves and hats perform for bundled-up neighbors on Park Avenue at an earlier Murray Hill holiday celebration.

events.title: Scandinavia House Holiday Concert & Lucia Procession
events.what: Members of New York’s Swedish community perform Scandinavian and American holiday songs, led by Ingrid Kullberg-Bendz. The hour-long program includes a traditional Saint Lucia procession with white gowns and glowing candles, plus an introduction to the holiday’s history.
events.where: Scandinavia House · 58 Park Avenue
events.when: December 6 and December 12, 2026, at 5 p.m.; approximately 60 minutes. These are two performances, not a daily run. Advance online tickets required.
events.cost: $30 general admission; $25 American-Scandinavian Foundation members. Check the ticket checkout for any additional booking fees.
events.imageAlt: Singers in white gowns with red sashes hold candles during an earlier Lucia performance; the central singer wears a candle crown.

events.title: Santa’s Secret
events.what: Explore eight holiday installations before a seated live-band cabaret and burlesque show in a Tribeca ballroom. About two hours; mature audiences 18+, and 21+ with ID for drinks. Tickets must be bought online; food and drinks are additional.
events.where: 62 Thomas Street, New York
events.when: November 13–December 30; select a dated session in the booking calendar.
events.cost: Regular tickets from $75 plus booking fees; limited 20% promotional offers currently show $60 + $3.89 booking fee for general seating. Prices vary by session; food and drinks extra.
events.imageAlt: A singer in a red dress performs with the Santa’s Secret band in an organizer photograph from an earlier production.

events.title: House of Yes Xmas Spectacular
events.what: The venue’s annual holiday variety show combines drag, dance, elaborate costumes and aerial performance. Adults 21+ only; performances contain adult themes. No re-entry.
events.where: House of Yes · 2 Wyckoff Avenue, Brooklyn
events.when: December 4; doors at 6:30 p.m.
events.cost: General-admission seating currently listed at $59.49; priority seating $70.30. Prices can change; table packages cost extra.
events.source: House of Yes; Fever ticket listing
events.imageAlt: Performers in red and green gift-box costumes on the House of Yes stage, in an earlier Xmas Spectacular photograph by Inna Shnayder.

events.title: Joy on the Farm: tree lighting and carols
events.what: Watch the farm’s holiday tree light up, then hear carols from the Queens Oratorio Society. The lighting and carols are explicitly free. Optional ticketed activities later include holiday hayrides, cookie decorating and lantern making; these are separate from the free core visit.
events.where: Queens County Farm Museum · 73-50 Little Neck Parkway
events.when: December 5; tree lighting 5:30 p.m., carols 5:45 p.m.; optional activities from 6 p.m.
events.cost: Tree lighting and carols free. Optional activity ticket: adults $10, ages 2–17 $15.
events.imageAlt: Visitors making holiday crafts at a long table inside Queens Farm, in an organizer photograph from an earlier celebration.

events.title: Old Stone House Holiday Artisans Bazaar
events.what: Browse handmade gifts, jewelry, accessories, art and homewares from Brooklyn makers around Washington Park. The outdoor bazaar includes music by DJ DiscoCzech and seasonal refreshments; shopping is optional. Extreme-weather date is December 6.
events.where: Old Stone House / Washington Park · 336 3rd Street and 4th Street Plaza at Fifth Avenue
events.when: December 5, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; extreme-weather date December 6.
events.cost: Free admission; gifts, cider and other purchases optional.
events.source: Brooklyn Pop-Up and Old Stone House
events.imageAlt: The stone-and-brick Old Stone House beside its garden, in the venue’s archival exterior photograph; this is the location, not a photograph of the upcoming bazaar.

events.title: Crafts at the Cathedral
events.what: Browse a juried fine-craft fair inside the Cathedral’s nave, with ceramics, jewelry, home accents and handmade gifts from artists around the country. Admission supports Cathedral community initiatives; purchases are optional once inside.
events.where: Cathedral of St. John the Divine · 1047 Amsterdam Avenue at 112th Street
events.when: December 4, 9:30 a.m.–7 p.m.; December 5, 9:30 a.m.–6 p.m.; December 6, noon–5 p.m.
events.cost: Adult single-day admission $15; seniors/students $12; weekend pass $22. Shopping extra.
events.source: Cathedral of St. John the Divine / Rose Squared
events.imageAlt: Craft stalls and visitors beneath the nave’s stone arches and rose window at an earlier Crafts at the Cathedral fair, in the Cathedral’s official photograph.

events.title: Holiday on the Hudson
events.what: A waterfront holiday gathering with live music, ornament making and hot chocolate while supplies last. Hear a brass quartet from the Harlem Chamber Players and watch the tree lighting at 5:30 p.m. Seating is limited and first come, first served; check weather updates before traveling.
events.where: West Harlem Piers · West 125th and Marginal Streets
events.when: December 5, 4:30–6 p.m.; tree lighting at 5:30 p.m. Rain date December 6.
events.cost: Free and open to the public; no required purchase.
events.source: Riverside Park Conservancy / Summer on the Hudson
events.imageAlt: An illuminated holiday tree beside the West Harlem waterfront at dusk, in the organizer’s photograph from an earlier season.

events.title: Frederic Church in Jamaica
events.where: Cooper Hewitt · 2 East 91st Street
events.when: October 30, 2026–February 15, 2027; daily 10am–6pm, except Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
events.cost: Currently $18 adult reduced admission during a gallery changeover; recheck ticket price before visiting. Pay-what-you-wish only 5–6pm daily.
events.what: More than sixty oil and graphite studies trace Church’s five months in Jamaica in 1865, from palms and ferns to mountain light. The exhibition places the landscapes in the context of the artist’s personal life and Jamaica under British colonial rule. Closed Thanksgiving, November 26.
events.imageAlt: The museum’s reproduction of Frederic Church’s Palm Trees, June 1865, showing palms on a Jamaican hillside.

events.title: Jessica Lichtenstein: Rewilding
events.where: Museum of Arts and Design · 2 Columbus Circle
events.when: May 30, 2026–April 18, 2027; Tuesday–Sunday, with Wednesday noon–8pm. Closed Mondays and November 26.
events.cost: General admission $20; seniors $16; students $14. Optional purchases extra.
events.what: An immersive third-floor installation brings forests, flowering canopies and ruins together with tiny female figures. Paintings, sculpture and video connect ecological imagination with feminist questions about autonomy and representation. The museum is closed on Thanksgiving and open November 27.
events.imageAlt: The Rewilding gallery at MAD, with colorful arched artworks on a green wall, a gold tree artwork on a purple wall and low sculptural blocks.

events.title: Wallabout Wonderland Holiday Market
events.what: The Brooklyn Navy Yard’s ninth annual holiday market gathers dozens of local makers for gifts, handmade goods, live performances and creative workshops inside the Duggal Greenhouse. Food, drinks and optional craft experiences are available for purchase. RSVP and a valid photo ID are required for entry.
events.where: Duggal Greenhouse, Building 362 · Brooklyn Navy Yard
events.when: December 5, 2026, noon–8 p.m. Advance RSVP recommended; same-day registration permitted. Under-18s must be accompanied by an adult and do not need photo ID.
events.cost: Free entry with RSVP; shopping, food, workshops/add-ons and parking cost extra. Parking must be booked by December 3.
events.source: Brooklyn Navy Yard / official Eventbrite ticketing
events.imageAlt: The empty Duggal Greenhouse event hall, with tall windows, pale steel roof trusses and an open concrete floor, photographed before an event setup.
